one_line: Browser-based accessible web editor where agents can build and audit front ends in one shared surface.
what_it_does: Combines multi-file editing, live preview, WCAG auditing, design-token checks, and WebMCP agent control.
leverage_rationale: The structured surface lets an agent edit, inspect live output, and run accessibility checks against shared state; generic UI driving would be markedly less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly joins editor, live preview, and WCAG audit for browser agents.
About text describes document.modelContext exposure and a closed build/audit loop.
execution_rationale: The Devpost packaging is coherent and the claimed scope is substantial, but the submitted video title is an unrelated Rick Astley video and no readable product frames were available as reliable end-to-end evidence.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows the unrelated Rick Astley video embed.
About text gives detailed feature claims but no usable transcript or verified product demo.
impact_rationale: Front-end builders and teams have a concrete accessibility and consistency problem, and integrating auditing into the build loop is directly valuable.
impact_evidence: Accessible-by-default positioning and WCAG 2.0-2.2 audit claims.
Design-system drift and breakpoint checks address real front-end workflow pain.
creativity_rationale: The shared editor-preview-audit-agent loop is a fresh synthesis with meaningful ambition beyond a chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Single-tab concept combines code, preview, audit, and agent collaboration.
Design token enforcement and accessibility-first workflow are distinctive together.
usability_note: Promising workflow, but evidence does not establish polish or reliability.
red_flags: Embedded video is titled Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up rather than a product demo.
No transcript and no readable product frames.
standouts: Accessibility is integrated as a first-class agent workflow rather than an afterthought.
Design-system and live-preview coupling is compelling.
advance_reason: Strong concept, but the apparent video mismatch and thin usable execution evidence prevent advancing.

one_line: Agent-authored personal learning courses with progress tracking and learning artifacts.
what_it_does: Uses WebMCP tools from an existing agent conversation to create courses, track progress, and generate artifacts for any subject.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools allow the agent to author and update durable course state and artifacts instead of merely explaining lessons in chat.
leverage_evidence: Pitch names course creation, progress tracking, and artifacts as WebMCP actions.
Screenshot packaging shows a dedicated Lore submission and demo media, though not the running app.
execution_rationale: The submission describes a coherent learning flow and reports a working app, but no submitted video and only limited packaging/gallery evidence cap confidence.
execution_evidence: About text explains course creation, progress, artifacts, and pedagogy warnings.
Devpost screenshot includes a Lore WebMCP Demo embed and coherent branding.
impact_rationale: Personalized learning is a clear use case with broad legitimate value, and the tool is aimed at making arbitrary subjects approachable.
impact_evidence: Explicit learner audience and Duolingo/Anki-inspired motivation.
Progress tracking and artifact generation support sustained learning.
creativity_rationale: Agent-authored curricula plus model-aware pedagogy feedback and artifacts is a fresh, ambitious learning interaction.
creativity_evidence: Learning happens in the existing agent conversation while the app provides structured course state.
Pedagogy warnings and progressive disclosure are thoughtful product ideas.
usability_note: The described flow is understandable, but visual proof of the actual learner experience is limited.
red_flags: Self-described vibe-coded implementation and limited proof of core flow.
standouts: Strong agent-as-author/teacher framing.
Specific model-oriented pedagogy safeguards.
advance_reason: Clear audience, credible value, and a meaningful structured-agent learning concept despite moderate evidence limits.

one_line: A live cooking board where a human and agent compose recipes and mutate shared state together.
what_it_does: Normalizes ingredients, composes and reorders recipe cards, and re-themes a shared recipe board through WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: The product's central idea is a shared visible board where agent actions mutate the same live state; this collaboration is substantially harder to reproduce with generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly says every action mutates the real DOM visible to both human and agent.
Seven typed tools and a parallel stdio MCP surface are described.
execution_rationale: The scope is tightly defined and the claimed tool contracts, normalization, headless visual check, and JSON-RPC test form unusually coherent evidence; screenshots show a polished recipe board, though no transcript.
execution_evidence: Devpost media preview visibly shows a recipe grid with cards, filters, tags, and match metadata.
About text reports end-to-end MCP JSON-RPC and visual checks.
Ingredient alias normalization and reversible visible state are specified.
impact_rationale: Home cooks have a real desire for flexible ingredient-based meal planning, and a collaborative agent can reduce friction and spark ideas.
impact_evidence: Concrete fridge-ingredient use case and recipe discovery UI.
Human-visible execution preserves trust and control.
creativity_rationale: The one-human/one-agent/one-board interaction and real-time re-theming are memorable and pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Agent acts on a shared board rather than replying in a bubble.
Live UI re-theming and invented cards extend beyond standard recipe chat.
usability_note: The visible card grid and explicit filters suggest a usable browsing experience.
red_flags: No transcript and video frame sheets show repeated UI states rather than clearly legible tool-call moments.
standouts: Strong shared-state WebMCP thesis.
Detailed typed-tool and canonicalization implementation.
advance_reason: One of the clearest examples of WebMCP changing the interaction model, with strong visual/product coherence.

one_line: Synthetic, session-only ledger for reviewing cash flow and drafting fictional entries with an agent.
what_it_does: Shows summary and filtered transactions and lets an agent create a human-reviewable draft entry without accounts or external integrations.
leverage_rationale: Strict, reversible tools make structured review and draft creation safer and more precise than ordinary UI automation, though the synthetic scope limits the delta.
leverage_evidence: Three narrowly scoped tools read summary, list transactions, and create a fictional draft.
Screenshot visibly shows dashboard, activity table, filters, and draft-entry flow.
execution_rationale: The product scope is intentionally narrow and coherently evidenced by a polished dashboard screenshot and explicit privacy/test claims.
execution_evidence: Visible media preview shows reserve summary, transaction table, filters, and draft flow.
About text states session-only in-memory state and focused evaluation harness.
impact_rationale: It is useful as a safe demonstration and learning tool for agent-mediated finance, but synthetic data means limited direct end-user impact.
impact_evidence: Explicitly targets safe exploration without accounts or real money.
Review-before-add boundary addresses trust concerns.
creativity_rationale: Privacy-first fictional finance is a thoughtful angle, though the ledger/dashboard concept itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Synthetic-only boundary and reversible draft workflow are deliberate.
WebMCP safety contracts are integrated into the demo.
usability_note: The visible dashboard is clear and appropriately scoped.
red_flags: No video frame sheets; screenshot is packaging/media preview rather than observed live execution.
standouts: Honest privacy and synthetic-data boundaries.
Clear reversible human-review flow.
advance_reason: Solid and honest demo, but narrower impact and less ambitious leverage than the strongest entries.

one_line: Agent-native freelance marketplace for structured discovery, evaluation, shortlisting, and proposal drafting.
what_it_does: Searches jobs and freelancers, checks reputation, manages shortlists, and creates proposal drafts while keeping submission human-controlled.
leverage_rationale: Structured marketplace data and authorization-aware tools materially outperform scraping for ranking, reputation checks, and safe drafting.
leverage_evidence: Eight WebMCP tools cover search, reputation, shortlist, and proposal drafts.
About text states tools use the existing authenticated session and Rails authorization rules.
execution_rationale: The stated Rails architecture and workflow are coherent, but demo_alive is unknown and the visual packet lacks reliable readable product proof.
execution_evidence: Detailed stack and tool description.
Video frame sheet submission is present but not relied on for a verified end-to-end completion.
impact_rationale: Clients and freelancers face real discovery and proposal friction; structured agent assistance can save time while preserving consequential human control.
impact_evidence: Two-sided audience and concrete marketplace tasks are explicit.
Human-only proposal submission is a credible safety boundary.
creativity_rationale: An agent-native two-sided marketplace is a fresh synthesis, especially with reputation and authorization-aware operations.
creativity_evidence: Agents support both clients and freelancers rather than only adding chat.
Draft-only boundary is integrated into marketplace design.
usability_note: Potentially useful, but login dependence and unknown live state increase friction.
red_flags: Authenticated workflow is not independently demonstrated in the packet.
standouts: Authorization-aware structured marketplace operations.
Good separation between drafting and final submission.
advance_reason: Strong real-world audience and meaningful WebMCP delta warrant advancement pending live verification.

one_line: Agent-assisted video clipping tool for finding precise moments and producing shareable clips.
what_it_does: Lets agents navigate video, locate moments, make cuts, and hand control back to a human editor; clips are stored and shared via Cloudflare infrastructure.
leverage_rationale: Precise temporal navigation and clip creation are tasks where structured tools can substantially reduce tedious UI manipulation while preserving human editing control.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on agent-assisted finding and cutting of video moments.
About text describes WebMCP plus manual editing and Cloudflare clip sharing.
execution_rationale: The revived product has a coherent purpose, credible prior domain experience, and a substantial implementation description, though packet evidence is not fully end-to-end.
execution_evidence: About text details React/TypeScript/Vite, Workers, Durable Objects, R2, and FFmpeg coordination.
Gallery_images=5 and submitted frame sheets indicate product evidence exists.
impact_rationale: Creators, gaming communities, and marketers have a concrete need for faster highlight extraction and sharing.
impact_evidence: Prior stated community of over 30,000 Tekken players and 5,000-gif workflow.
Social clip creation is an identifiable recurring pain.
creativity_rationale: The hands-in-the-goop human-agent editing model is a strong, memorable application of WebMCP to temporal media work.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human craft clips together rather than replacing the editor.
Revival of a specialized clipping workflow with agent collaboration.
usability_note: Precision editing is promising, but the packet does not establish the full interaction quality.
red_flags: Project explicitly revives an eight-year-old tool, making origin eligibility uncertain.
standouts: Strong domain-specific agent collaboration use case.
Credible prior user/community context.
advance_reason: High-value and creative workflow with a substantial WebMCP delta; eligibility and live execution need verification.

one_line: Interactive ASCII art gallery of poetic, responsive works and visiting minds.
what_it_does: Presents a browsable gallery of named ASCII artworks with an interactive, atmospheric interface.
leverage_rationale: The packet describes an interactive gallery but provides little evidence that WebMCP materially changes creation or browsing compared with normal UI interaction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch is simply an interactive ASCII art gallery.
Devpost packaging lists 14 gallery images but does not establish agent-specific capability.
execution_rationale: The large set of titled works and gallery evidence suggest a coherent, authored art experience, though the central workflow and agent behavior are not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About text lists many distinct titled pieces.
Facts report 14 gallery images and an alive demo.
impact_rationale: It offers niche artistic and contemplative value to audiences interested in experimental web art, but practical audience/problem fit is less explicit.
impact_evidence: Gallery contains a substantial set of original titled works.
Interactive art and creative expression are legitimate forms of impact.
creativity_rationale: The poetic ASCII gallery concept and unusual work titles indicate a distinctive artistic direction pursued beyond a generic template.
creativity_evidence: Named works such as The Wall Changes Its Mind and Starlight Pressure create a coherent imaginative world.
ASCII art is used as the primary medium rather than decoration.
usability_note: Gallery browsing appears viable, but interaction details are not evidenced here.
red_flags: No video frame sheets and no clear WebMCP functionality in the packet excerpt.
standouts: Distinctive authored ASCII-art world.
Strong poetic naming and gallery concept.
advance_reason: Creative art experience, but insufficient demonstrated WebMCP relevance for this challenge.

one_line: WebMCP-powered portfolio context manager that turns visitor goals into evidence, takeaways, and reviewed briefs.
what_it_does: Ranks relevant portfolio work, creates visible visitor briefings, saves takeaways, and prepares editable inquiries without sending them.
leverage_rationale: Canonical structured portfolio evidence plus visitor-context-aware ranking is much more reliable than scraping pages, while human confirmation governs durable or outbound actions.
leverage_evidence: Five tools are described for profile, evidence ranking, briefing, takeaway, and project brief creation.
About text explicitly contrasts structured canonical facts with presentation-oriented scraping.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and carefully bounded with visible, reversible actions, but no video transcript and limited direct runtime proof reduce confidence.
execution_evidence: About text specifies confirmation before unguessable-link takeaway and never-sent contact form.
Frame sheets and five gallery images indicate a substantial presentation packet.
impact_rationale: Recruiters, founders, CTOs, and design leaders have a real problem turning portfolio browsing into relevant evidence and next steps.
impact_evidence: Specific professional audiences and workflow pain are articulated.
Tailored evidence and editable briefs directly address repeated context loss.
creativity_rationale: The portfolio-as-context-manager framing is a fresh synthesis that uses agent context without surrendering human review.
creativity_evidence: Visitor-specific durable takeaway and project brief are more ambitious than a contact-form chatbot.
Canonical evidence and honest gaps are built into the interaction.
usability_note: Human review and reversible actions are good usability choices; live proof remains limited.
red_flags: No transcript and no fully verifiable end-to-end demo in the packet.
Durable public takeaway introduces privacy/consent complexity, though confirmation is described.
standouts: Excellent evidence-first portfolio workflow.
Strong human-control boundaries for public and outbound actions.
advance_reason: Clear audience, strong WebMCP leverage, and a differentiated professional workflow.

one_line: Governed WebMCP runtime that dynamically exposes relevant tools and requires approval for consequential actions.
what_it_does: Virtualizes capabilities by task, shows before/after plans, executes with approval, verifies outcomes, issues receipts, and supports rollback.
leverage_rationale: Capability virtualization, shared live state, approval boundaries, idempotent execution, verification, and rollback directly address limitations of static agent tool surfaces; the intended governance model is impractical as a simple UI-driving layer.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes dynamic registration of five relevant tools from 79, tombstones, approval boundaries, receipts, verification, and rollback.
Demo scenario covers rescue planning and a refund with before/after state and human authorization.
execution_rationale: The transcript provides unusually complete end-to-end evidence: discover state, propose a plan, authorize, execute once, verify consequences, and show receipts across two domains.
execution_evidence: Video transcript explicitly narrates a completed rescue and verified refund workflow.
Quantified baseline comparison: 79 tools/28,894 bytes versus 5 tools/3,776 bytes.
Frame sheets and Devpost packaging correspond to a titled Agentdesk demo.
impact_rationale: Agent safety, tool overload, approval, and auditability are urgent problems for teams deploying agents in business applications; the demonstrated governance directly addresses them.
impact_evidence: Business shipping/refund scenario shows financial and customer-state consequences.
Runtime supports receipts, verification, rollback, and human reconciliation.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic capability virtualization with task-aware tool surfaces, structured tombstones, and verified reversible execution is an ambitious and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Same runtime spans fictional rescue operations and ordinary business workflows.
Approval-required return semantics and commit-time re-checking are unusually deep governance design.
usability_note: The focus and approval model should improve operator trust, though dynamic tools add conceptual complexity.
red_flags: Demo status is marked unknown despite strong video evidence.
Claims are presented through a staged demo, so production generality is not established.
standouts: Exceptional end-to-end evidence and quantified tool-surface reduction.
Human approval, verification, receipts, and rollback form a complete governance story.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP leverage, complete demonstrated execution, and high-impact governance problem make this the strongest entry in the packet.

one_line: Shared heat-emergency planning board where humans set constraints and agents draft and stress-test accountable plans.
what_it_does: Combines map/dashboard state with structured tools for allocation planning, route inspection, constraint application, stress tests, and human review.
leverage_rationale: The agent handles multi-variable combinatorial planning over the same live map and operational state the human controls, then stops at explicit human review; generic UI driving would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Six focused tools read context, inspect centers/routes, apply constraints, draft deterministic plans, stress-test disruptions, and request review.
About text reports plan HG-001 appearing immediately on the map/dashboard with audit trail.
execution_rationale: The synthetic planning scenario is coherent and includes concrete outputs, constraints, stress testing, and a human approval boundary; visual packet supports a substantial dashboard but lacks transcript.
execution_evidence: Reported plan metrics: 97.7% coverage, 98% equity, $40,700 spend, 2.7-mile average trip, zero violations.
Bridge-closure stress test and visible audit trail are described.
Frame sheets and two gallery images were submitted.
impact_rationale: Heat emergencies create real coordination problems for public agencies and community responders, and the proposed human-agent planning workflow targets a high-stakes need.
impact_evidence: Specific coordinator audience and concrete constraints: risk, capacity, routes, budget, accessibility, bridges.
Human approval and synthetic-data disclaimer appropriately bound the prototype.
creativity_rationale: The shared local-reality-plus-combinatorial-agent model is an ambitious and socially meaningful application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Human pins local reality while agent stress-tests plans on a live operations board.
Deliberately omitting an approval tool reinforces the governance concept.
usability_note: Dashboard and map outputs sound actionable, but high-stakes operational usability is not fully observed.
red_flags: Synthetic fictional city and no transcript limit real-world validation.
No direct evidence of a live agent invocation in the supplied text.
standouts: Concrete quantified planning and stress-test outputs.
Strong human authority boundary for a high-stakes domain.
advance_reason: High-impact, technically meaningful shared-state planning workflow with strong evidence of intended end-to-end behavior.
